- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (especially if sentiment drops post-spike) — adjust downward bias.
- Overshoot downward trends in low sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — avoid premature decline, add slight upward bias.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is 5%+ above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment drops 2–3 days before forecast peak, anticipate downward correction.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overreact to short-term sentiment swings — dampen volatility in later days.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is high but price is falling, don’t assume continuation; add caution factor.
